title: Why your strength potential might be limiting your size gains
summary: NH explains that strength does not equal size, although well-programmed long-term strength progression does bring size. Lifters gifted with good leverages get stronger easily and chase low-rep numbers without growing. They then ignore advice from weaker lifters and end up as unhappy fake powerlifters. They should train for reps, variation and tonnage instead.
claims: Strength does not equal size; they are different values with cross-pollination, and training for one is not training for the other
The fitness industry swung from bodybuilders saying strength does not matter to people saying only strength matters; both are wrong
If you train like a powerlifter you will look like a powerlifter: built to perform, not necessarily aesthetic
Strength largely depends on leverages; long arms visibly predict a good puller, while size potential is revealed only with time
People who pull 400 lb on their first gym visit usually have good leverages or are gifted for strength
Bigger legs do not mean a bigger squat between two people, but if one person's legs grow from 20 to 25 inches, his squat has increased
Strength progression gives immediate gratification, which is why NH encourages tracking progress through your lifts
Focusing only on the strength number makes you forget it was meant to serve size, and you drift onto a powerlifter's path
Gifted lifters who chase low-rep strength get good technically but accumulate little tonnage
A skinny guy who overhead presses 150 lb for 3 has strength potential far above normal but may have smaller shoulders than a one-plate presser doing far more volume
The one-plate overhead presser may do five times the tonnage of the gifted lifter
For a naturally weak lifter like NH, a 225 lb overhead press would mean massive shoulders, but for a strength-gifted lifter it may produce nothing
Gifted strength lifters often give up on size, assuming they cannot grow, when training for reps and tonnage would bring size gains
Because we judge advice by strength, gifted lifters stop listening to the 99% of lifters weaker than them
Many 'fake powerlifters' secretly want aesthetics but settle for strength because it comes easily and earns praise, leaving them bitter and passionless
Do not let natural abilities dictate your rep scheme; accumulate tonnage and use variations rather than only a minimalist main movement
NH is naturally weak, so for him strength gains translate to size; for strength-gifted lifters the relationship is skewed and strength potential limits size
